questions.q: A long-hidden painting called ‘Iris’ sold for €50 million in Paris on Thursday, a French auction record. Which Impressionist painted it?
questions.e: Accept Monet. Sotheby’s Paris, 22 October: about US$56 million, smashing the estimate. If you said Manet, one vowel just cost you €50 million.

questions.q: Disney+ and Hulu greenlit a reboot of which Ryan Murphy musical series, originally set at an Ohio high school?
questions.e: Confirmed 21 October. Cast and date TBC. Slushies at the ready.

questions.q: LeBron James made his debut for his fourth NBA team on opening night, beating the Knicks 106–100. Which team?
questions.e: Accept the Sixers or Philadelphia. 20 October (US time), kicking off a record 24th season at 41. Some of us need a lie-down after one.

questions.q: Ahead of the US Grand Prix, Guinness certified the world’s largest what at Austin’s Circuit of the Americas?
questions.e: Accept hat. Unveiled 19 October, about 13 metres wide and 5 metres tall. Yee-haw, as they say in Austin.

questions.q: Barcelona’s 11-game winning run ended with a 4–2 Champions League defeat to which club on Tuesday?
questions.e: Accept PSG or Paris. 20 October at the Parc des Princes. The holders don’t do hospitality.

questions.q: The Orionid meteor shower peaked this week. It’s made of debris from which famous comet?
questions.e: Accept Halley. Peak around 21–22 October. Not Hailey, not Haley’s. Spelling counts in space.

questions.q: Two teams who have never won a World Series are meeting in this year’s. Name both.
questions.a: Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays
questions.e: Need both; Brewers and Rays will do. Set on 20 October when the Rays won the ALCS. A first-time champion is guaranteed.

questions.q: Champions League newcomers from which Italian lakeside city thrashed Manchester United 4–1 on Wednesday?
questions.e: Accept Como 1907. 21 October. The scenery is lovely; the scoreline less so, if you’re United.

questions.q: Researchers say which undeciphered 15th-century manuscript, held at Yale, may have been bound in the wrong order?
questions.e: Accept Voynich. Study published 19 October. Still unreadable, just possibly unreadable in a different order.

questions.q: Japan’s MMX probe launched this week to collect samples from which moon of Mars?
questions.e: Launched on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima on 20 October (Japan time). Not Deimos, though it gets a flyby. Samples due home in 2031.

questions.q: A rare coin of ‘Olaf the Holy’ turned up in a Viking hoard. He was king, and is now patron saint, of which country?
questions.e: Reported 21 October from the Mørstad hoard near Rena. Fewer than 20 of his coins were known. Not Denmark. Not Sweden. Close, though.

questions.q: This weekend is Phillip Island’s last MotoGP. Which city’s street circuit takes over the Australian round from 2027?
questions.e: Accept Adelaide. Phillip Island hosts its final race this weekend, 23–25 October; Adelaide gets a city-centre track from November 2027.

questions.q: Archaeologists think a medieval abbot was buried in a recycled Roman sarcophagus at which famous London church?
questions.e: Reported 21 October: probably Abbot Aelfwig, who died around 1020. Recycling, the medieval way.

questions.q: Before opening night, the New York Knicks raised a banner for their first NBA title in how many years?
questions.e: Accept 53. 20 October (US time). Their previous title was in 1973. Patience is a virtue; 53 years is a lifestyle.

questions.q: South Africa ran a 7.6 km, 696-wagon iron-ore train this week, breaking which Australian miner’s 25-year-old record?
questions.e: Accept BHP Billiton or BHP Iron Ore. Transnet’s train ran on 18 October; BHP’s 2001 train had 682 wagons over 7.35 km. Mind the level crossing.

questions.q: The Brewers are in their first World Series since which year?
questions.e: Accept 1982. Confirmed 20 October. They lost that one to St Louis, in seven. No pressure.

questions.q: Which Argentine scored twice and set up another in Como’s 4–1 win over Manchester United?
questions.e: Accept Paz. 21 October: a goal inside two minutes, an assist, then another. Busy night.

questions.q: Jacob Misiorowski threw the fastest pitch in World Series history in Friday’s Game 1. To the nearest mph, how fast?
questions.e: Accept 103 or 104 mph (about 166 km/h). His first pitch, 23 October. The Brewers won 3–2. The batter is still looking for it.

questions.q: How many grams of Phobos does Japan’s MMX mission aim to bring back to Earth?
questions.e: Accept 10, or ‘at least 10’. Launched 20 October. Small jar, long trip: home in 2031.

questions.q: The little rover riding along on Japan’s Phobos mission is called Idefix, after a comic-strip dog. What is that dog called in English?
questions.e: Obelix’s dog in Asterix. The French-German rover launched with MMX on 20 October. Idéfix is a pun on ‘idée fixe’. Melted yet?

questions.q: Which Major League Baseball team won the first World Series title in its history this week, beating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games?
questions.e: Accept the Brewers or Milwaukee. Game 5 finished 4–1 on 28 October (US time); catcher William Contreras was named series MVP. If you said the Rays, they managed exactly one win, so close-ish.

questions.q: Which England captain won the men’s Ballon d’Or at a ceremony in London on Monday?
questions.e: Accept Kane. 26 October at the London Palladium, after 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England. Took him a while to collect silverware; now he needs a bigger shelf.

questions.q: Who won the women’s Ballon d’Or on the same night, playing for Barcelona and London City Lionesses?
questions.e: Accept Putellas. 26 October in London; Ewa Pajor was second and Khadija Shaw third. Her third Ballon d’Or, for those keeping score at home.

questions.q: The NFL played its first ever regular-season game in France this week. In which city?
questions.e: Accept Saint-Denis or the Stade de France. 25 October: Steelers 16, Saints 10, in front of 78,488 fans. Aaron Rodgers called La Marseillaise ‘gorgeous’. Ooh la la.

questions.q: The world’s heaviest jack-o’-lantern, carved from a 3,156 lb (1,431 kg) pumpkin, went on show this week in which Massachusetts town famous for its witches?
questions.e: Unveiled on Salem Common on 26 October, with the mayor proclaiming 27 October ‘Great Pumpkin Day’. Grown by Ron Wallace in Rhode Island. Roughly the weight of two dairy cows, minus the mooing.

questions.q: Apple unveiled its first Mac with an OLED screen this week. What else can that MacBook Pro screen do for the first time on a Mac?
questions.e: Accept touchscreen or touch. Announced 28 October, on sale 6 November from US$2,899. The glowing Apple logo is back too. Fingerprints on your MacBook, coming soon.

questions.q: Dictionary.com named its 2026 Word of the Year on Monday. Which internet word means pushing something to the max, as in ‘sleep___’?
questions.e: Accept maxing. Announced 26 October; runners-up included ‘affordability’ and ‘unc’. We are quizmaxxing right now.

questions.q: Which Canadian pop star’s single ‘Housewife’ debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Global 200 this week?
questions.e: Accept McRae. Chart dated 31 October (revealed 27 October). It stalled at No. 2 on the US Hot 100, behind Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’, which notched a record-extending 25th week at the top.

questions.q: Which Kazakh world No. 1 defended her Ningbo Open title on Sunday, thrashing Leylah Fernandez 6–2 6–2?
questions.e: Accept Rybakina. 25 October, her first trophy as world No. 1 and a tour-leading fourth of 2026. Fernandez blinked and it was over.

questions.q: Scientists in Yunnan, China, named a giant new fungus that grows up to 50 cm tall ‘Dianjunus ___’. Fill in the blank, inspired by a famous dinosaur.
questions.e: Reported 27 October. Pale yellow, finger-shaped and grows on oak roots; it needed a whole new fungal family. A mushroom with king-sized ambition.

questions.q: Which space telescope found dusty water ice on the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, in a study reported this week?
questions.e: Accept Webb or JWST. Reported 26 October, led by Dr Silvia Protopapa. The visitor from another star turns out to look rather like our own icy worlds beyond Neptune. Even aliens do frost.

questions.q: India women swept a three-match ODI series 3–0 on Wednesday against a team they had never played in international cricket before. Which African nation?
questions.e: 28 October in Vadodara, an eight-wicket win, with spinner Vaishnavi Sharma taking five wickets. First date, three-nil. Harsh.

questions.q: Yuri Yoshida came from four shots back to win her first LPGA title at the BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea on Sunday. Which country is she from?
questions.e: 25 October at Pine Beach Golf Links, Haenam, 17 under, one shot clear. If you guessed Korea, the home crowd agrees with you; the scorecard does not.

questions.q: Astronomers led by MIT’s Dr Lynn Matthews say the atmosphere of which red supergiant in Orion has recovered from its ‘Great Dimming’ of 2019–20?
questions.e: Reported 28 October. Its little companion star, Siwarha, tears through the giant’s atmosphere ‘like a jet boat through a lake’. Beetlejuice, Beetlejuice, Beet… no, don’t.

questions.q: Scientists revealed hidden glazes on the 37,000-year-old Chauvet Cave paintings without touching the walls. What kind of light did they shine on them?
questions.e: Accept UV. Reported 28 October from the Ardèche in France. An orange glow suggests some lines were drawn with burning-hot charcoal. Prehistoric artists: always lit.

questions.q: Kateřina Siniaková won the Japan Women’s Open in Osaka on Sunday while ranked 86th in singles. In which form of tennis is she ranked world No. 1?
questions.e: 25 October, a 6–1 6–0 demolition of Ashlyn Krueger in 68 minutes, ten years after losing the Osaka final. Turns out she’s handy without a partner too.

questions.q: A cupboard in a house on Pompeii’s Via dell’Abbondanza held 24 childhood charms and 38 bronze coins. The skeletons of two baby what were found in a nearby amphora?
questions.e: Accept wood mice. Reported 29–30 October. The charms (crepundia) were designed to rattle. The mice were probably after a snack and picked the worst possible week.

questions.q: A garden whose gates warn ‘These plants can kill’ was recognised by Guinness on 27 October for most species in a poison garden. In which Northumberland town is it?
questions.e: Accept Alnwick Garden. Created by Jane Percy, Duchess of Northumberland, inspired by a Medici poison garden in Italy. Look, don’t lick.

questions.q: NASA asked companies this week how they would boost the Hubble Space Telescope’s orbit. To at least what altitude, in kilometres?
questions.e: Accept 600. Request issued 29 October; replies due 30 November, mission by 2032. Hubble has been sinking for years, which is relatable.

questions.q: A rhino-sized dinosaur from a Surrey brickworks, named this week, is called Paludohadros proudlovii. The ‘Paludo’ part comes from a Latin word meaning what?
questions.e: Accept marsh, bog or wetland. Published 27 October; senior author Prof Susannah Maidment of the Natural History Museum, London. It was found about 100 m from the famous Baryonyx. Swamp duck, basically. Melted yet?

questions.q: Zoo Atlanta showed off its new arrivals Ping Ping and Fu Shuang on Friday. What kind of animal are they?
questions.e: Accept pandas. Public debut 6 November, after flying in from Chengdu in September on a 10-year loan. If you said koalas, wrong bear-shaped thing, wrong continent.

questions.q: Who became Formula 1’s youngest ever world champion in Mexico City on Sunday?
questions.e: Accept Andrea Kimi Antonelli or Antonelli. 1 November: third place was enough for the Mercedes driver at 20 years and 68 days, beating Sebastian Vettel’s 2010 mark of 23. Some of us were still working out how to parallel park at 20.

questions.q: Collins Dictionary named its 2026 Word of the Year on Tuesday: a slang term for outshining someone. What is it?
questions.e: Accept mog. Announced 3 November; it grew out of ‘AMOG’, alpha male of the group. Last week Dictionary.com picked ‘maxxing’. The dictionaries are mogging each other now.

questions.q: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat Atlanta 16–0 on Sunday. How many passes did they complete?
questions.e: Accept zero or 0. 1 November: Baker Mayfield went 0 for 3, and the Bucs ran for a franchise-record 324 yards instead. First team to win without a completion since the 1974 Buffalo Bills. Who needs hands?

questions.q: Detroit’s Claude P. Moore spent 11 years building a 5,251 kg record breaker, confirmed by Guinness this week. A record what?
questions.e: Accept rubber-band ball. Announced 3 November: 11,578 lb, crushing the old 9,032 lb record. Roughly elephant-sized, and considerably bouncier.

questions.q: NASA’s twin ESCAPADE spacecraft were due to slingshot past Earth on Saturday and Monday, firing their engines over southern Australia. Where are they heading?
questions.e: First flyby 7 November, second on 9 November; arrival in September 2027. If you said the Moon, aim higher. About 380 times higher.

questions.q: Which team won the WNBA title in only their second season, beating the Atlanta Dream 68–63 in Game 7 last Saturday?
questions.e: Accept the Valkyries or Golden State. 31 October, the franchise’s first championship. Year one: learn the playbook. Year two: lift the trophy. Show-offs.

questions.q: Melbourne Cup winner Point of Law was bought from the royal stable of which monarch?
questions.e: Accept King Charles or Charles. 3 November at Flemington, ridden by Ethan Brown; trainer Ciaron Maher became the first in the race’s 166 years to train the first three home. The King may want a word with his bloodstock agent.

questions.q: Which band scored its first ever No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 this week, 20 years after the album came out?
questions.e: Accept MCR. The Black Parade leapt from No. 139 to No. 1 on the chart dated 7 November, after a 20th-anniversary reissue; it peaked at No. 2 in 2006. The longest wait for a No. 1 album ever. Not a phase, Mum.

questions.q: Edinburgh Zoo confirmed capybara triplets this week. Their big brother Bru was named after which famous Scottish fizzy drink?
questions.e: Confirmed 4 November: two boys and a girl, born 28 October to Luna and Rodney, names wanted from the public. Bru was the first capybara born in Scotland in 18 years. Not whisky. They’re babies.

questions.q: Which Australian qualifier knocked Novak Djokovic out of the Paris Masters on Wednesday?
questions.e: Accept Hijikata. 4 November, 2–6 6–3 6–3. A qualifier beating a 24-time Grand Slam champion: the scoreboard had to check itself twice.

questions.q: Britain’s Harriet Dart won her first WTA singles title on Sunday, coming through qualifying. In which Chinese city?
questions.e: 1 November, beating Austria’s Lilli Tagger 4–6 6–3 6–4. Seven matches, 20 sets, and a few saved match points along the way. If you said Beijing or Shanghai, close, but no trophy.

questions.q: Which NASA observatory, named after a fast-flying bird, burned up in the atmosphere on Wednesday after about 22 years hunting gamma-ray bursts?
questions.e: Accept the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. Re-entered 4 November, launched in 2004. Solar activity puffed up the upper atmosphere and dragged it down. Not Falcon. Not Sparrow. Swift, swiftly.

questions.q: Kenya’s Sheila Chepkirui won the women’s New York City Marathon on Sunday. Men’s winner Andreas Almgren, in his first ever marathon, is from which country?
questions.e: 1 November, in 2:06:01. Chepkirui won her second New York title in 2:24:36, with America’s Jess McClain six seconds behind. First marathon, first place. The rest of us would settle for finding the start line.

questions.q: Which Champions League club, managed by Cesc Fàbregas, won 9–1 away at Lens on Wednesday?
questions.e: Accept Como 1907. 4 November: an eight-goal margin equals the modern Champions League record, and only Bayern had scored nine in a game before. Lake Como: lovely views, brutal hosts.

questions.q: Catalan writer Cristina Fernández Cubas won the top prize in Spanish-language literature on Tuesday. It’s named after the author of Don Quixote. What is it?
questions.e: Accept Premio Cervantes or Miguel de Cervantes Prize. Announced 3 November; worth €125,000, and she is only the seventh woman to win it. If you said the Quixote Prize, you tilted at the wrong windmill.

questions.q: Tottenham captain Drew Spence set a new record for Women’s Super League appearances on Sunday, passing Millie Bright. How many WSL games has she now played?
questions.e: Accept 217. 1 November, in a 4–1 win at Birmingham. She spent 14 years at Chelsea before Spurs. That’s a lot of shin pads.

questions.q: A newly named prehistoric rodent that weighed about 30 kg, Yakamys sirindhornae, was named after a princess of which country?
questions.e: Reported 6 November: 33–35 million years old and known from just two teeth found in a Krabi coal mine in 2004 by geologist Pannipa Tian. About half a capybara. Sleep well.

questions.q: Mexico City’s Day of the Dead parade marked its 10th edition last Saturday. Which 2015 James Bond film inspired it?
questions.e: 31 October. The film opened with Bond strolling through a skeleton-filled Mexico City parade that didn’t exist; the city liked it so much it started a real one in 2016. Life imitates art, then adds marigolds.

questions.q: France’s most famous literary prize, the Prix Goncourt, went to Philippe Jaenada on Tuesday. How much prize money does the winner get, in euros?
questions.e: Accept €10. Announced 3 November at the Drouant restaurant in Paris. The glory, and the sales, are worth rather more. Spend it wisely. Melted yet?

questions.q: SpaceX tried to catch both halves of its giant rocket with the launch tower’s ‘chopsticks’ on Friday. What is the rocket called?
questions.e: Flight 15, 13 November (US time) from Starbase, Texas. The Super Heavy booster aborted its catch and ended up in the Gulf of Mexico, while the ship carried on into orbit. Half a double catch is still a catch. Sort of.

questions.q: Which giant monster’s new film, subtitled Minus Zero, opened at No. 1 at the North American box office last weekend?
questions.e: Accept Godzilla Minus Zero. About US$31.6 million over 6–8 November, nearly three times what Godzilla Minus One opened with in 2023. If you said King Kong, wrong lizard. Wrong ape, even.

questions.q: Who won F1’s São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos last Sunday, his second win there in a row?
questions.e: Accept Norris. 8 November, in a wet-dry-wet race, with Max Verstappen charging from 21st on the grid to second. Rain, chaos, and still a McLaren on top.

questions.q: Canadian human rights lawyer Stephanie Case became the first woman to run 100 continuous miles on which continent, this week?
questions.e: Reported 13 November, at the Antarctica Ice Ultra: 38 laps of a 4.2 km loop, in temperatures dropping below −30 °C, and sunburn from the midnight sun. Meanwhile you’re complaining about the walk to the car.

questions.q: A Guinness World Record making news this week belongs to a Los Angeles artist who paddled 26.37 miles from Catalina Island in a kayak grown from what?
questions.e: Accept mycelium or fungus. Reported 12 November: Sam Shoemaker’s 12-foot boat took seven weeks to grow and 12 hours to paddle. Record: longest solo journey by a fungal mycelium boat. A fun guy. Sorry.

questions.q: The SS United States, still holder of the transatlantic speed record for passenger liners, was deliberately sunk off Florida on Wednesday to become the world’s largest what?
questions.e: Accept reef. 11 November, in about 55 m of water off Destin. At 302 m it’s longer than the Titanic, and it beats the old record-holder, the aircraft carrier USS Oriskany. Fish have never had it so roomy.

questions.q: Which country singer’s Choosin’ Texas spent a record-extending 27th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, announced on Monday?
questions.e: Accept Langley. Billboard reported it on 9 November; no song has spent longer at the top. Mariah’s Christmas song can only dream of that many Decembers.

questions.q: Researchers at Germany’s University of Tübingen reported on Thursday that which black birds make visual decisions about twice as fast as humans?
questions.e: Accept carrion crows. Published in Science, 12 November: about 235 milliseconds on a moving-dot task, roughly twice as quick as humans and monkeys. Bird brain is now a compliment.

questions.q: Greenpeace sank a 1.5-tonne limestone boulder into the North Sea on Thursday to block bottom trawlers. Which famous broadcaster was it carved to look like?
questions.e: Accept Attenborough or Sir David. 12 November, in the Southern North Sea marine protected area. Nicknamed the ‘Attenboulder’. A national treasure, now also a national paperweight.

questions.q: This week’s WTA Finals moved from Riyadh to which Californian desert venue?
questions.e: Accept Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Running 8–15 November with the world’s top eight women. If you said Palm Springs, you’re close enough to see it, but no.

questions.q: At 81, M. John Harrison became the oldest Booker Prize winner on Monday. His novel’s cheerful title is The End of… what?
questions.e: 9 November in London. Picked unanimously by a panel chaired by Mary Beard; he’s also the first winner to come out of the science fiction world. £50,000 and a title that sounds like Monday morning.

questions.q: Marie-Antoinette Katoto scored a hat-trick on Wednesday as which French club thrashed Juventus 6–0 in Turin in the Women’s Champions League?
questions.e: Accept OL Lyonnes or Olympique Lyonnais. 11 November: three goals inside 52 minutes, and Juve barely got a shot on target. Turin, lovely city. Bring a helmet.

questions.q: Which became the first US airline on Wednesday to ban AI agents from booking tickets for its customers?
questions.e: Accept United. Announced 11 November, citing privacy and rules such as passengers personally confirming what’s in their bags. Your robot can browse. You still have to click ‘buy’.

questions.q: Archaeologists said this week that about 8,000 frog bones found in a Roman-era ditch near Cambridge were probably left by which birds?
questions.e: Accept short-eared owls. Reported 10 November by Bournemouth University and MOLA: frogs eaten during a young-frog boom about 1,700 years ago, with hen harriers probably roosting nearby. Not a Roman frog feast. Toga party cancelled.

questions.q: Francesca Clapcich became the first woman to win the IMOCA Globe Series after finishing which solo transatlantic race to Guadeloupe on Thursday?
questions.e: Accept Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe. 12 November: eighth across the line after 11 days 11 hours, despite a broken bowsprit on day five. Sailing alone across an ocean, with damage. Try that on a pedal boat.

questions.q: Mercedes clinched the 2026 F1 constructors’ championship in Brazil. How many constructors’ titles has the team now won?
questions.e: Accept nine. Sealed 8 November, after eight in a row from 2014 to 2021, and a week after Kimi Antonelli took the drivers’ title. If you said seven, that’s Lewis Hamilton’s drivers’ titles. Wrong trophy cabinet.

questions.q: A butterfly treated as a single species for about 200 years turned out, in a study out Thursday, to be how many species?
questions.e: Accept 3. 12 November in Zootaxa, led by Florida Museum doctoral student Anisha Sapkota: ultraviolet wing patterns and DNA gave them away. The new one is Colobura cryptica. Hidden in plain sight for two centuries.

questions.q: On Remembrance Day this week, Lillooet broke a 109-year-old November heat record. Which Canadian province is it in?
questions.e: Accept BC. 11 November: 20.3 °C beat 19.4 °C from 1917, one of 32 records broken or tied that day, as Vancouver and Victoria also hit record highs. Shorts in November, in Canada. Who knew.

questions.q: Jessica Pegula knocked fellow American Coco Gauff out of the WTA Finals on Thursday by beating which Czech player in three sets?
questions.e: Accept Noskova. 12 November: 7–6 4–6 7–5, saving a match point in nearly three hours. Gauff won her own match and still went home. Tennis maths is cruel.

questions.q: Sam Shoemaker’s record mushroom kayak was grown from the mycelium of which genus of bracket fungus, the same one as reishi?
questions.e: The species was Ganoderma polychromum (confirmed 12 November). Reishi, or lingzhi, is a Ganoderma too. If you said Agaricus, that’s the supermarket button mushroom, and it would have sunk. Melted yet?

questions.q: The sandwich is named after an 18th-century Earl of where?
questions.e: Not a trick. Mostly.

questions.q: ‘Kangaroo’ entered English in 1770 from ‘gangurru’, a word in which Aboriginal language of far north Queensland?
questions.e: Recorded by Cook’s crew at the Endeavour River, near today’s Cooktown.

questions.q: Which country invented paper?
questions.e: Around 2,000 years ago. Credit usually goes to Cai Lun.

questions.q: The QWERTY layout was designed for which machine?
questions.e: Accept typewriter. Long before your laptop.

questions.q: LEGO comes from the Danish ‘leg godt’. What does that mean?
questions.e: Accept play well. Stepping on one is not playing well.

questions.q: Velcro was inspired by what clinging to a Swiss engineer’s dog after a walk?
questions.e: Accept burdock burrs or seeds. George de Mestral, 1940s.

questions.q: Bubble wrap was first invented in 1957 as what?
questions.e: Accept wallpaper. Nobody wanted it. Then everybody did.

questions.q: Post-it Notes came from a failed attempt to make a super-strong what?
questions.e: Accept adhesive or glue. Spencer Silver at 3M.

questions.q: What does the Japanese word ‘emoji’ mean?
questions.e: Accept picture plus character or picture letter. Nothing to do with emotion. Mind blown.

questions.q: The word ‘robot’ comes from a 1920 play by a writer from which country?
questions.e: Accept Czech Republic or Czechia. Karel Čapek’s R.U.R.

questions.q: Jeans are named after which Italian city, where the cloth was made?
questions.e: Denim comes from ‘de Nîmes’, in France.

questions.q: The croissant’s crescent-shaped ancestor, the kipferl, came from which country?
questions.e: Accept Austria or Vienna. France just made it flakier.

questions.q: Which Australian science agency developed key Wi-Fi technology in the 1990s?
questions.e: Accept CSIRO.

questions.q: The microwave oven was invented after radar melted what in engineer Percy Spencer’s pocket?
questions.e: Accept chocolate or a candy bar. 1945.

questions.q: Which board game was first called Lexiko, then Criss-Crosswords?
questions.e: Alfred Butts, an out-of-work architect, 1930s.

questions.q: In Italian, the @ symbol is called ‘chiocciola’. What animal is that?
questions.e: Accept snail. Look at it. It’s a snail.

questions.q: The Frisbee is named after a bakery whose empty pie tins students threw. What was the bakery called?
questions.e: Accept Frisbie or Frisbie Baking Company. Bridgeport, Connecticut.

questions.q: The word ‘pyjamas’ came into English from which language?
questions.e: Accept Hindi, Urdu or Persian. ‘Leg garment’.

questions.q: Monopoly grew out of ‘The Landlord’s Game’, patented in 1904 by which woman?
questions.e: Accept Elizabeth Magie. She designed it to show how landlords got rich. Decades later, a man sold a version to Parker Brothers.

questions.q: The word ‘nerd’ first appeared in print in a 1950 children’s book by which author?
questions.e: ‘If I Ran the Zoo’. Accept Theodor Geisel. Nerdy of you to know.

questions.q: Which continent has no countries at all?
questions.e: Plenty of claims. Zero countries. Lots of penguins.

questions.q: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.e: Kicking Sicily, apparently.

questions.q: Which city sits on two continents, Europe and Asia?
questions.e: Accept Istanbul. Not Constantinople. Not any more.

questions.q: Lake Hillier in Western Australia is famous for being which colour?
questions.e: Algae and salt. Not food colouring.

questions.q: Which is the world’s largest lake by area?
questions.e: Accept Caspian. A sea in name only.

questions.q: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.e: Accept Lesotho. Eswatini only nearly.

questions.q: Which African country was formerly called Abyssinia?
questions.e: Ethiopia was long known abroad as Abyssinia. It’s one of the few African countries never colonised.

questions.q: Which is the only country whose national flag is neither a rectangle nor a square?
questions.e: Two stacked triangles. Rule-breaker.

questions.q: Which Bolivian city is the world’s highest seat of government?
questions.e: About 3,640 metres up. Bring a jumper.

questions.q: Counting overseas territories, which country has the most time zones?
questions.e: Twelve. Russia has eleven. Thanks, overseas territories.

questions.q: Australia is wider from east to west than which body’s diameter?
questions.e: Accept Moon. About 4,000 km versus 3,474 km.

questions.q: Which country has the most islands?
questions.e: Over 260,000. Accept Sweden only. Not the Philippines. Not Indonesia.

questions.q: Which US state is closest to Africa?
questions.e: Not Florida. Look at a globe, not a flat map.

questions.q: Point Nemo, the place furthest from any land, is in which ocean?
questions.e: Accept South Pacific. Nearest humans are often on the space station.

questions.q: Bir Tawil is land that no country claims. Which two countries is it between?
questions.e: Need both. Neither wants it, for complicated reasons.

questions.q: Name a country whose flag shows a map of the country itself.
questions.e: Accept Cyprus or Kosovo.

questions.q: Which river flows through more countries than any other?
questions.e: Accept Danube. Ten countries, four capitals.

questions.q: Which two countries are the only doubly landlocked ones in the world?
questions.e: Need both. Surrounded only by other landlocked countries.

questions.q: What is the world’s southernmost national capital?
questions.e: Accept Wellington, New Zealand. About 41 degrees south.

questions.q: Which country shares France’s longest land border?
questions.e: Via French Guiana. 730 km, longer than the border with Spain. Melted yet?

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.e: Two for the gills, one for everything else. Overachiever.

questions.q: What is the only mammal capable of true powered flight?
questions.e: Flying squirrels are just very committed gliders.

questions.q: What is a group of flamingos called?
questions.e: Yes, really. Nature has a sense of occasion.

questions.q: Which living bird lays the largest egg?
questions.e: About 1.4 kg. That’s a lot of omelette.

questions.q: Polar bear fur looks white. What colour is the skin underneath?
questions.e: Good for soaking up sun. Bad for hiding from a photographer.

questions.q: What unusual shape is wombat poo?
questions.e: Accept cubes or square. Useful for marking territory, since it doesn’t roll away.

questions.q: What is the largest animal ever known to have lived?
questions.e: Bigger than any dinosaur we’ve found. Accept blue whale only.

questions.q: Which seahorse parent carries the babies until they hatch?
questions.e: Accept dad. Equal parenting, sort of.

questions.q: Which bird is the fastest in a dive, topping 300 km/h?
questions.e: Accept peregrine. Your hatchback is not impressed.

questions.q: Koalas eat almost nothing but the leaves of which tree?
questions.e: Accept gum tree. It’s not very nutritious, which explains the sleeping.

questions.q: Male platypuses have what venomous body part on their hind legs?
questions.e: A sting a person won’t forget. Duck-bill, beaver tail, and also this.

questions.q: Honeybees tell each other where food is by doing which dance?
questions.e: Accept waggle. Karl von Frisch won a Nobel for decoding it.

questions.q: How many chambers does a cow’s stomach have?
questions.e: One stomach, four rooms. Accept four only.

questions.q: The smiling axolotl is native to lakes near which capital city?
questions.e: Accept Mexico. Never quite grows up, like some of your friends.

questions.q: What is a group of crows called?
questions.e: Crows would like a word with their publicist.

questions.q: Which animal has the largest eyes in the world, roughly dinner-plate size?
questions.e: Accept giant squid if you’re feeling generous. Good for spotting sperm whales.

questions.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.e: Lives in a pocket. No rent.

questions.q: Which is the only bird family that can fly backwards?
questions.e: Accept hummingbird. Wings blur at dozens of beats a second. Show-offs.

questions.q: Which tiny, nearly indestructible animal is nicknamed the ‘water bear’?
questions.e: Accept tardigrade. It has survived the vacuum of space.

questions.q: Which vertebrate is the longest-living known, estimated at around 400 years or more?
questions.e: Radiocarbon dating of eye lenses, 2016. One may have been swimming about when Shakespeare was writing.

questions.q: Which fruit is the base of guacamole?
questions.e: Yes, a fruit. Don’t let your toast tell you otherwise.

questions.q: What is the seaweed wrapped around sushi called?
questions.e: Accept nori only. Not ‘the green paper’.

questions.q: What is the main ingredient of hummus?
questions.e: Accept garbanzo beans. Tahini takes second billing.

questions.q: By weight, which spice is usually the most expensive in the world?
questions.e: Picked by hand from crocus flowers. Accept saffron. Pricey, like your last brunch.

questions.q: Which cheese belongs in a traditional Greek salad?
questions.e: It’s a protected name, and the Greeks will mention it.

questions.q: Paella comes from which Spanish region?
questions.e: Chorizo in it is a diplomatic incident.

questions.q: Marzipan is made from which nut?
questions.e: Accept almond. Sculpted into fruit, for reasons.

questions.q: Botanically, peanuts aren’t nuts. What are they?
questions.e: Accept pulses or beans. Peas in a pod, underground.

questions.q: Earl Grey tea gets its flavour from the oil of which citrus fruit?
questions.e: Tastes like a very posh aftershave. In a good way.

questions.q: Kimchi is usually made from which fermented vegetable?
questions.e: Accept napa or wombok cabbage. Korea’s national mood lifter.

questions.q: The Italian dessert name tiramisu translates roughly as what?
questions.e: Accept lift me up or cheer me up. All that coffee helps.

questions.q: Which natural food famously keeps for thousands of years without spoiling?
questions.e: Found edible in ancient Egyptian tombs, reportedly. Don’t eat tomb food.

questions.q: What is Spain’s traditional sparkling wine called?
questions.e: Champagne’s cheerful cousin.

questions.q: Which country drinks the most coffee per person?
questions.e: Accept Finland. It’s dark up there. Italy is nowhere near the top.

questions.q: Which spirit goes in a classic Bloody Mary?
questions.e: Technically a breakfast food. Technically.

questions.q: What does the Scoville scale measure?
questions.e: Accept chilli heat. Bell pepper scores zero. Your pride, likewise.

questions.q: The Caesar salad was invented in a restaurant in which Mexican city?
questions.e: By Caesar Cardini, an Italian-American. Not Rome. Julius had nothing to do with it.

questions.q: Sachet ‘wasabi’ outside Japan is mostly which other root?
questions.e: Plus green food colouring. You’ve been played.

questions.q: Fresh apples float in water. What makes them float?
questions.e: About a quarter of an apple’s volume. Hence bobbing.

questions.q: The Hawaiian pizza, with ham and pineapple, was invented in 1962 in which country?
questions.e: By Greek-born Sam Panopoulos in Ontario. Hawaii is entirely innocent.

questions.q: Which red-leafed Christmas plant is named after a US diplomat who brought it back from Mexico?
questions.e: Joel Poinsett, 1820s. Those red ‘petals’ are actually leaves.

questions.q: Which band sang Last Christmas?
questions.e: And you’ve just lost Whamageddon. Sorry.

questions.q: Who wrote A Christmas Carol?
questions.e: 1843. Bah, humbug to anyone who said Scrooge.

questions.q: Who played Kevin in Home Alone?
questions.e: Accept Culkin. Burglars hated him.

questions.q: Which reindeer has the shiny red nose?
questions.e: He began in a US department store’s 1939 giveaway booklet.

questions.q: In Japan, which fast-food chain is a hugely popular Christmas meal?
questions.e: Thanks to a 1970s ad campaign. Accept Kentucky Fried Chicken. Book ahead.

questions.q: Which horned Alpine figure comes for naughty children around Christmas?
questions.e: Santa’s bad cop. Coal looks fine by comparison.

questions.q: A French bûche de Noël is a cake shaped like what?
questions.e: Accept Yule log. Edible firewood.

questions.q: In The Twelve Days of Christmas, what are the five?
questions.e: Accept golden rings. The most sensible gift by a distance.

questions.q: Which Christmas spice, often stuck into oranges and hams, is the dried flower bud of a tree?
questions.e: Accept clove. Looks like a tiny nail, which is where the name comes from.

questions.q: The Catalan nativity figure called the caganer is doing what?
questions.e: Trousers down, tucked away in the scene. Accept the rude word. It’s tradition.

questions.q: What is the name of the skyscraper in Die Hard?
questions.e: Accept Nakatomi. And yes, it’s a Christmas film. Next argument please.

questions.q: In what year was All I Want for Christmas Is You released?
questions.e: Mariah Carey. Back every year since, like the tax office.

questions.q: Who composed The Nutcracker?
questions.e: Accept Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky. Sugar plums courtesy of a celesta.

questions.q: Ded Moroz, ‘Grandfather Frost’, brings presents in which country?
questions.e: Accept Russia. His granddaughter Snegurochka helps.

questions.q: Which Swedish town’s giant Christmas straw goat is famous for being set on fire?
questions.e: Accept Gavle. Burnt many times since 1966. It’s illegal, and it keeps happening.

questions.q: Who sang the best-selling version of White Christmas?
questions.e: Accept Crosby. Among the best-selling singles ever recorded.

questions.q: Traditional British mince pies originally contained what?
questions.e: Accept minced meat. Now it’s just fruit, and the name stays.

questions.q: In Italian folklore, which kindly old witch brings children gifts on the night of 5 January?
questions.e: A kindly witch on a broomstick. Accept Befana.

questions.q: Which festive song was the first ever played in space, in 1965?
questions.e: Gemini 6 astronauts Wally Schirra and Tom Stafford, on a tiny harmonica and bells, after reporting a mystery red-suited object.

questions.q: Which planet has the shortest day, at about 10 hours?
questions.e: Biggest and fastest. Bit smug about it.

questions.q: Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the solar system, is on which planet?
questions.e: About two and a half times the height of Everest.

questions.q: Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe?
questions.e: About 78%. Oxygen only gets the credit.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.e: From aurum. Not Go, not Gd, not ‘bling’.

questions.q: Roughly how fast does light travel, in kilometres per second?
questions.e: Accept close enough. Your internet should be so lucky.

questions.q: Bananas are slightly radioactive because of which element?
questions.e: A tiny amount. Please continue with your smoothie.

questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.e: Accept mercury only. Hold the thermometer jokes.

questions.q: Seen from space, what colour is the Sun?
questions.e: It only looks yellow through our atmosphere. Crayons have misled you.

questions.q: What are clouds mostly made of?
questions.e: Accept water. Not fluff. Not candyfloss.

questions.q: Which is hotter, a bolt of lightning or the surface of the Sun?
questions.e: About five times hotter. Stay off the golf course.

questions.q: Diamonds are made of which element?
questions.e: Same as pencil lead, with far better marketing.

questions.q: Does sound travel faster in air or in water?
questions.e: More than four times faster. Whales are not surprised.

questions.q: What is the name for the claim that hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold?
questions.e: After a Tanzanian schoolboy who noticed it making ice cream in the 1960s. Scientists still argue.

questions.q: What is absolute zero in degrees Celsius, to the nearest degree?
questions.e: Accept -273.15. Cold enough to make Canada blush.

questions.q: Which scale ranks minerals by scratch hardness, from talc to diamond?
questions.e: Accept Mohs. Friedrich Mohs, 1812. Fingernail scores about 2.5.

questions.q: Which planet has a day that’s longer than its year?
questions.e: Turns so slowly it’s basically a teenager on a Sunday.

questions.q: Which colour is on the outside edge of a primary rainbow?
questions.e: Inside is violet. Now say Roy G. Biv and feel better.

questions.q: Polonium is named after which country?
questions.e: Marie Curie’s homeland, which wasn’t on the map at the time.

questions.q: What is the study of fungi called?
questions.e: Accept mycology only. A very fun guy’s degree.

questions.q: Which two letters of the alphabet appear nowhere on the periodic table?
questions.e: Need both. Check it yourself. We’ll wait.
